'''John David Maitland Wright''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|FRSE}} (20 May 1942 &ndash; 7 August 2023) was a British [[mathematician]], specialising mainly in [[functional analysis]] and [[operator theory]]. 

==Early life and education==
Wright was born on 20 May 1942, the son of Phyllis (née Harris) and mathematician [[E._M._Wright| Sir Edward Maitland Wright]]. He went to [[Aberdeen Grammar School]] and subsequently studied mathematics at the [[University of Aberdeen]]. <ref name="uaberdeen"></ref> 

Wright graduated with first class honours from University of Aberdeen in 1964. For his postgraduate studies he went to [[Christ Church, Oxford]] where he obtained his doctorate in 1967. <ref name=mathgene></ref> For his thesis on [[measure theory]], Wright was awarded the Oxford Senior Mathematical Prize and Johnson Prize. <ref name="lmsnewsletter"></ref> 

==Career==

In 1965 Wright was appointed to a junior college lectureship at Christ Church and in 1968 became the Leathersellers’ Tutorial Fellow in Mathematics at [[St Catherine’s College, Oxford]].<ref name="lmsnewsletter"></ref> 

In 1971, at the age of 28, he was appointed professor of [[pure mathematics]] at the [[University of Reading]] and later became head of department.<ref name="lmsnewsletter"></ref> 

Wright was treasurer of the [[London Mathematical Society]] from 1986 to 1994 and  deputy director of the [[Isaac Newton Institute]] in Cambridge from 1994 to 1996.<ref name="uaberdeen"></ref> 

In 2004 he was appointed to a Sixth Century Chair at the [[University of Aberdeen]] which he held until his retirement in 2015. Subsequently he became senior associate [[research fellow]] of [[Christ Church, Oxford]] until 2021.<ref name="uaberdeen">{{cite web|url=https://www.abdn.ac.uk/staffnet/news/22243/|title = Professor John David Maitland Wright FRSE|website=[[University of Aberdeen]]}}</ref>

Wright worked mainly in [[functional analysis]], [[measure theory]], [[operator theory]] and related areas, including applications to [[quantum mechanics|quantum theory]]. He published over 130 papers in mathematical journals. <ref name="lmsnewsletter"></ref><ref name="mathscinet">{{cite web|url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/MRAuthorID/184710|title = Wright, John David Maitland|website=[[American Mathematical Society]]}}</ref> A significant part of Wright's research work was on [[AW*-algebra|AW*-Algebras]] and monotone complete C*-algebras culminating in a book coauthored with Kazuyuki Saito. <ref name="lmsnewsletter"></ref> Other notable work include results on [[Jordan operator algebra|Jordan C*-Algebras]] in 1977 and a solution of the Mackey-Gleason Problem in 1994 (with L.J. Bunce).<ref name="lmsnewsletter"></ref>

==Honours ==
Wright was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 1978 <ref name="uaberdeen" /><ref name="lmsnewsletter">{{cite journal |last1=Cho |first1=Cho-Hu |date= |title= Obituaries of Members: John D. M. Wright 1942-2023 |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/default/files/inline-files/NLMS_509_for%20web.pdf |journal=LMS Newsletter |volume=509 |issue= December 2023|pages=39–40 |doi=10.1112/NLMS |doi-broken-date=12 July 2025 |access-date=December 6, 2023}}</ref><ref name="frse">{{cite web|year=2016 |title=RSE Fellows as at 15/03/2016 |url=https://www.royalsoced.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/lists/fellows.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330014912/https://www.royalsoced.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/lists/fellows.pdf |archive-date=30 March 2016 |website=[[Royal Society of Edinburgh]]}}</ref> and Foreign (Honorary) Academician of the Società Nazionale di Scienze, Lettere e Arti in Napoli in 1994. <ref name="lmsnewsletter"></ref>
